paragraphs.source_en: In the blink of an eye, spring arrived in the eighteenth year of Keichō, and Ōkubo Nagayasu was suddenly struck by a sense of how brief life was. The events of recent years, together with the unending deaths of people he knew well, had saddened even so self-assured a man as he.

paragraphs.source_en: Just as unease began to stir in Nagayasu, Ōgimachi Suemitsu died, followed by Ōtomo Yoshinori and Naitō Nobunari; one after another, those close to him vanished from the world.

paragraphs.source_zh: 正当长安心生不安之时，正亲町季秀随之故去，然后是大友义乘、内藤信成，和他亲近之人接连不断从这世上消失了。

paragraphs.source_en: By the eighteenth year of Keichō, life and death themselves seemed to prowl around Nagayasu. On the twenty-fifth day of the first month, Ikeda Terumasa, a kinsman of his wife, died at the age of fifty. Amano Yasukage, who had worked closely with Nagayasu in affairs of government, died in the middle of the second month. Soon afterward, Aoyama Tadanari, the former Kantō magistrate and a relative of Nagayasu by marriage, passed away; Koide Yoshimasa of Osaka also died, aged forty-nine.
